focus: Verifying that an allocation satisfies the minimum interception probability constraint
problem_text: Given 3 targets and an interception-probability threshold alpha=0.8. Single-missile hit probabilities are p1=0.5, p2=0.4, p3=0.6. A candidate allocation is x=(3,4,2). Given that allocating k missiles to target i yields total interception probability P_i(k)=1-(1-p_i)^k, prove that target 1 meets the requirement, i.e. P_1(3) >= alpha.

focus: Verifying that an allocation satisfies the minimum interception probability constraint
problem_text: Given 4 targets and threshold alpha=0.75, with a common single-missile hit probability p=0.3 and candidate allocation x=(4,4,3,3). Given P_i(k)=1-(1-p)^k, prove that target 3 fails the requirement, i.e. P_3(3) < alpha.

focus: Verifying that an allocation satisfies resource and priority constraints
problem_text: There are m=15 missiles with priority T1>T2>T3, requiring x1>=x2>=x3 and at least 2 missiles per target. Candidate allocation is (7,5,3). Prove that this allocation satisfies the total-count, priority, and lower-bound constraints xi>=2.

focus: Verifying logical consistency of a threat-evaluation relation
problem_text: In an air-defense system each aerial target is evaluated by speed v (Mach) and altitude h (km). Define 'threat not lower': target A is not lower than B iff vA >= vB and hA <= hB (faster and lower means greater threat). Define 'strictly higher': A is strictly higher than B iff A is not lower than B and (vA > vB or hA < hB). Prove that 'strictly higher' is transitive: for any A, B, C, if A is strictly higher than B and B strictly higher than C, then A is strictly higher than C.

relations.strictly_higher: (vA >= vB ∧ hA <= hB) ∧ (vA > vB ∨ hA < hB)

assumptions: Speed and altitude are positive reals
partial order based on componentwise comparison

focus: Verifying mutual exclusivity of multi-sensor fusion rules
problem_text: A sensor-fusion system classifies targets with three rules: Rule 1 (ballistic missile): max speed > 5 Mach and apogee > 50 km. Rule 2 (cruise missile): max speed <= 5 Mach and a sustained low-altitude segment exists (altitude < 1 km). Rule 3 (UAV): max speed <= 5 Mach and no sustained low-altitude segment. Prove that for any target the premises of any two rules cannot hold simultaneously (rules are mutually exclusive, so classification is unique).

focus: Verifying mutual exclusivity of electronic-reconnaissance rules
problem_text: Electronic-reconnaissance classification rules: Rule 1 (AWACS): pw > 500 and f <= 3 GHz. Rule 2 (fighter radar): pw <= 500 and f > 3 GHz. Rule 3 (jammer): pw > 500 and f > 3 GHz. Prove the three rules are pairwise mutually exclusive.
assumptions: Radiated power and frequency are positive reals

focus: Proving injectivity of a greedy allocation algorithm
problem_text: There are n incoming targets (ordered by descending threat priority) and m interceptors (m <= n). The fire-allocation algorithm assigns interceptors with increasing index to targets in priority order, so the assignment f : Fin m -> Fin n is strictly increasing: for any i j : Fin m, if i < j then f(i) < f(j). Prove that any strictly increasing assignment is injective: for any i j : Fin m, if f(i)=f(j) then i=j.

focus: Proving (by pigeonhole) that m<n precludes full coverage
problem_text: There are n incoming targets and m interceptors with m < n (not enough ammunition). Prove that no surjective assignment exists from m interceptors to n targets, i.e. there is no f : Fin m -> Fin n such that for every target j : Fin n some interceptor i : Fin m satisfies f(i)=j. Equivalently, when ammunition is strictly fewer than targets, at least one target is unassigned.

focus: Proving an injectivity property of the greedy allocation algorithm
problem_text: There are n incoming targets and m interceptors (m <= n). A greedy algorithm assigns them in priority order. Prove that the assignment produced by the algorithm is an injection from a subset of targets to the interceptor set, i.e. distinct targets get distinct missiles and each missile is assigned at most once.

focus: Proving conflict-freeness of a tactical decision table
problem_text: A tactical doctrine selects interceptor type by target speed v and altitude h: Condition 1 (long-range): v >= 3 and h >= 20. Condition 2 (short-range): v <= 1 and h <= 3. Prove conflict-freeness: for any positive reals v and h, Conditions 1 and 2 cannot both hold, i.e. not((v >= 3 and h >= 20) and (v <= 1 and h <= 3)).
assumptions: Speed and altitude are positive reals

focus: Proving conflict-freeness of a tactical decision table
problem_text: Decision table: Condition 1 (active intercept): p >= 0.8 and r >= 5. Condition 2 (abandon): p <= 0.2 and r <= 1. Prove conflict-freeness: not((p >= 0.8 and r >= 5) and (p <= 0.2 and r <= 1)).
assumptions: Interception probability and ammunition reserve are positive

focus: Proving completeness of a tactical decision table
problem_text: A tactical doctrine selects interceptor type by speed v and altitude h: Condition 1 (long-range): v >= 3 and h >= 20. Condition 2 (short-range): v <= 1 and h <= 3. Condition 3 (medium/default): neither Condition 1 nor 2. Prove completeness: for any positive reals v and h at least one condition holds, i.e. (v >= 3 and h >= 20) or (v <= 1 and h <= 3) or (not(v >= 3 and h >= 20) and not(v <= 1 and h <= 3)).
assumptions: Speed and altitude are positive reals
default rule covers all unmatched cases

focus: Proving infeasibility of a resource-constrained allocation
problem_text: Given 3 targets, each needs at least 1 and at most 2 interceptors, with m=7 missiles total. Let the allocation be (x1,x2,x3) with x1+x2+x3=7 and 1<=xi<=2. Prove that no feasible allocation exists, i.e. the constraint system is infeasible.

focus: Deciding optimality of a weapon-target allocation, proof or counterexample
problem_text: Given 10 identical missiles to be allocated among three target classes (carrier, destroyer, frigate). Allocation variables (x1,x2,x3) satisfy x1+x2+x3=10 and xi nonnegative integers. Threat weights are W1=3, W2=2, W3=1; single-missile hit probabilities are P1=0.1, P2=0.05, P3=0.2. The expected payoff is F(x1,x2,x3)=3*(1-0.9^x1)+2*(1-0.95^x2)+1*(1-0.8^x3). For candidates (5,2,3) and (6,2,2), decide whether F(5,2,3) >= F(6,2,2); prove it or give a counterexample.
assumptions: Interception events on one target are independent
a hit counts the batch as destroyed

focus: Deciding optimality of a weapon-target allocation, proof or counterexample
problem_text: Given 7 missiles to allocate between two targets with threat weights W1=3, W2=4 and single-missile hit probabilities P1=0.5, P2=0.3. F(x1,x2)=3*(1-0.5^x1)+4*(1-0.7^x2). Compare (2,5) and (3,4); decide whether F(2,5) >= F(3,4).

focus: Proving optimality via the diminishing-marginal-gain condition
problem_text: Simplified WTA: n=2, v1=3, v2=2, p1=p2=0.5, m=3. Define marginal gain g_i(k)=v_i*p_i*(1-p_i)^k. For allocation x=(2,1), prove that for any integer allocation y with y1+y2=3 and yi>=0, F(2,1) >= F(y1,y2), where F(a,b)=3*(1-0.5^a)+2*(1-0.5^b).

focus: Proving optimality via the diminishing-marginal-gain condition
problem_text: Simplified WTA: n=2, v1=2, v2=2, p1=p2=0.5, m=2. Marginal gain g_i(k)=v_i*p_i*(1-p_i)^k. For x=(1,1), prove F(1,1) >= F(y1,y2) for all y1+y2=2, where F(a,b)=2*(1-0.5^a)+2*(1-0.5^b).

focus: Proving a lower bound on required interception probability
problem_text: A high-value target requires interception probability at least 0.9 with single-missile hit probability p=0.4. Allocating k missiles gives P(k)=1-(1-p)^k. Prove that 4 missiles are insufficient, i.e. P(4) < 0.9.

focus: Proving a lower bound on required interception probability
problem_text: A high-value target requires interception probability at least 0.9 with single-missile hit probability p=0.4. P(k)=1-(1-p)^k. Prove that 5 missiles suffice, i.e. P(5) >= 0.9.

focus: Proving concentrated allocation beats uniform allocation
problem_text: Two targets with threat values v1=4, v2=1, hit probability p=0.5, and m=4 missiles total. F(a,b)=v1*(1-(1-p)^a)+v2*(1-(1-p)^b). Compare concentrated (3,1) with uniform (2,2); prove F(3,1) > F(2,2).

focus: Proving concentrated allocation beats uniform allocation
Proving residual threat falls below threshold for a two-stage scheme
problem_text: A target undergoes two-stage interception: stage 1 fires 2 long-range missiles (hit probability p1=0.3), stage 2 fires 3 short-range missiles (p2=0.5). Threat value v=10. Residual threat is R=v*(1-p1)^k1*(1-p2)^k2. Prove R < 1.
assumptions: missiles within a stage are independent

focus: Proving residual threat falls below threshold for a two-stage scheme
problem_text: A target undergoes two-stage interception: stage 1 fires 3 long-range missiles (p1=0.5), stage 2 fires 3 short-range missiles (p2=0.5). Threat value v=20. Residual threat R=v*(1-p1)^k1*(1-p2)^k2 with k1=3, k2=3. Prove R < 0.5.
assumptions: missiles within a stage are independent

focus: Proving reachability of a safe path through a threat field
problem_text: An interceptor operates in a 2024-row by 2023-column combat-airspace grid. 2022 cells hide enemy threat sources. The interceptor starts in some cell of the first row and each step moves to a cell in the next row. It passes safely as long as it avoids threat cells. Prove that no matter how the 2022 threat sources are placed, the interceptor can always find a safe path from the first row to the last row.
constraints: 不能进入威胁源所在格
assumptions: Threat positions are fixed but unknown
all columns between adjacent rows are reachable

focus: Proving existence of a safe jump order avoiding interference points
problem_text: There are n aerial targets of distinct threat values a1,...,an with total s=a1+...+an. The enemy places n-1 interference points M={m1,...,m_{n-1}} (not containing s) along a route. Starting from the origin, the interceptor jumps successively toward a1,...,an in some order, each jump distance being the target's threat value. Prove there exists a jump order such that the interceptor never lands on any interference point.

focus: Proving an upper bound on the fraction of acute triangles
problem_text: A radar detects 100 aerial targets, no three collinear. Any three form a triangle; a triangle whose three interior angles are all acute is called an effective interception triangle. Prove that the number of effective interception triangles is at most 70% of all triangles.
assumptions: an acute triangle corresponds to full-coverage formation

focus: Proving existence of pairwise-disjoint cyclic shifts of a subset
problem_text: Let A be the interception-coverage region of 101 fire units, an 101-element subset of S={1,2,...,10^6}. Prove there exist 100 shifts t1,...,t100 in S such that the shifted regions Aj={x+tj : x in A} (j=1..100) are pairwise disjoint.

focus: Proving a balanced partition of interceptors across two fire units
problem_text: There are 4n interceptors numbered 1..4n (the number is the combat-power value). Each is labeled with one of n models, exactly 4 per model. Prove the 4n interceptors can be split between two fire units so that (1) the two units have equal total combat power and (2) each unit has exactly 2 missiles of each model.

focus: Proving reachability of radar on/off states under adjacent flips
problem_text: There are 2n radar stations (n>=1), numbered 1..2n, each on or off. An operation picks station i (1<=i<=n) and flips stations i and i+1. Initially all 2n are on. Prove that after finitely many operations exactly k stations can be on, determine all reachable k (k has the same parity as n and n<=k<=2n), and characterize all reachable k.

focus: Proving existence of a set with exactly m unit-distance neighbors per point
problem_text: Prove that for any positive integer m there exists a finite set S of radar sites such that every site s in S has exactly m other sites at distance 1 (one standard communication-distance unit).
constraints: 每个站点恰好m个等距邻居

focus: Proving a Schur-type additive relation among 6-coloring of 1..1978
problem_text: An air-defense alliance has 1978 units numbered 1..1978 in 6 service branches. Prove that within some single branch there are 3 units such that one unit's number equals the sum of the other two (or one equals twice another in the same branch).

focus: Proving an upper bound on 3-term-AP-free selections
problem_text: From n incoming targets (numbered 1..n) select m to track such that no three selected numbers form an arithmetic progression. Prove the maximum m is at most floor((n+1)/2).

focus: Proving existence of an all-high-threat sub-rectangle
problem_text: Color every cell of an (a+b+1)x(a+b+1) combat-airspace grid 'high threat' or 'low threat', with a,b positive integers. Given at least a^2+ab-b high-threat cells, prove there is an (a+1)x(b+1) sub-rectangle whose cells are all high-threat.
assumptions: each cell is high or low

focus: Proving eventual periodicity of a max-recurrence sequence
problem_text: Let a1,a2,... be a positive-integer sequence (radar tracking signal strength). Suppose there is a positive integer N such that for all n>N, a_n = max{a_{n-1}, a_{n-2}}. Prove the sequence is eventually periodic with period 1 or 2, and determine all possible limiting behaviors.
assumptions: recurrence holds from some index onward

focus: Proving bounds for a difference-array assessment hierarchy
problem_text: In a multi-level assessment system, n bottom sectors each report a threat value (a permutation of 1..n). Each upper level takes the absolute difference of two adjacent lower values, aggregating upward to a single top value. Prove each level's outputs are bounded by a value depending on n, and analyze how the bottom permutation affects the maximum differences.
assumptions: bottom row is a permutation of 1..n

focus: Proving a lower bound on detector-node count
problem_text: Deploy detector nodes on an n x n radar grid so that (a) every undeployed cell shares an edge with a deployed cell (covered), and (b) every deployed cell shares an edge with an undeployed cell (non-redundant). Prove the number of deployed nodes is at least ceil(n^2/3).
constraints: 条件a: 空格邻接探测节点
条件b: 探测节点邻接空格

focus: Proving existence of an equal-sum partition
problem_text: From 10 target batches of distinct two-digit positive-integer threat values, prove one can select two disjoint groups with equal total threat value.
assumptions: Threat values are distinct two-digit positive integers

focus: Determining the valid parameter set for a grid-labeling scheme
problem_text: Label each integer lattice point of the plane with a positive integer (site number) such that (1) for every positive integer M only finitely many points have label < M, and (2) each point's label is at most c times the maximum label of its four up/down/left/right neighbors. Determine all positive reals c for which such a labeling exists.

focus: Proving an angle inequality in an acute triangle
problem_text: Let ABC be an acute interception triangle (interceptors at A, B, C), O its circumcenter, and P the foot of the altitude from A to BC. Given angle BCA >= angle ABC + 30 degrees, prove angle CAO > angle OAP.
assumptions: P is the foot of the altitude from A to BC

focus: Proving angle BAC is acute from an obtuse distance triangle
problem_text: Three targets form triangle ABC and an interceptor sits at point P. If PA, PB, PC form an obtuse triangle with PA the longest side, prove angle BAC is acute.
assumptions: P is any point in the plane

focus: Proving the Schur inequality for triangle side lengths
problem_text: Let a,b,c be the side lengths of an interception triangle (distances between three fire units). Prove a^2 b(a-b)+b^2 c(b-c)+c^2 a(c-a) >= 0 and determine the equality condition.

focus: Proving a parameter bound for a nonnegative superposition signal
problem_text: Define the radar superposition function f(x)=1-a cos x-b sin x-A cos 2x-B sin 2x with real parameters a,b,A,B. Given f(x)>=0 for all phase x, prove a^2+b^2+A^2+B^2 <= 2.

focus: Proving the optimal partition bound for a target-trajectory sequence
problem_text: Let a1,...,an be n radar observations of a target trajectory. For each 1<=i<=n define the split deviation di=max{aj:1<=j<=i}-min{aj:i<=j<=n} (difference of the prefix maximum and suffix minimum), and let d=max{di:1<=i<=n}. Prove that there exists a reordering of the sequence such that d equals max{aj:1<=j<=n}-min{aj:1<=j<=n}.

focus: Proving a power-sum bound for a bounded nondecreasing sequence
problem_text: Let x0,x1,x2,... be a nondecreasing real sequence with 0<=x0<=x1<=... and partial sums sum_{i=0}^{m-1} x_i <= 1 for all m>=1. Prove that for every positive integer k, sum_{i=0}^{inf} x_i^k <= 1 + 1/(k-1), and determine when equality holds.

focus: Proving the maximum product decomposition of a fixed resource total
problem_text: Split 1976 units of air-defense resource among several fire units (each gets at least 1). Total combat power is the product of the units' resource counts. Prove that power is maximized when the counts are as close to 3 as possible, and find this maximum.
assumptions: Combat power is the product of resource counts

focus: Proving existence of a fourth-power product subset
problem_text: An air-defense system identifies 1985 distinct targets; each target's radar feature code is a positive integer whose prime factors all lie in {2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23}. Prove there exist 4 targets whose feature-code product is a fourth power of an integer.
assumptions: product of 4 codes is a fourth power

focus: Proving bounds on a three-site combined-effect expression
problem_text: Three air-defense sites have resource allocations x,y,z (nonnegative reals) with x+y+z=1. Define the combined effect E=xy+yz+zx-2xyz. Prove 0<=E<=7/27 and analyze the equality conditions.

focus: Proving an existence condition for a weighted allocation scheme
problem_text: Let the allocations of five fire-power grades be x1,...,x5 (nonnegative reals). The first-order weighted sum satisfies x1+2x2+3x3+4x4+5x5=a, and the fifth-order weighted sum satisfies x1^5+2x2^5+3x3^5+4x4^5+5x5^5=a. Prove that such an allocation exists only when a satisfies a specific condition.

focus: Proving an equal-sum partition of consecutive integers
problem_text: There are n+1 target batches (n>=100) with threat values n, n+1, ..., 2n. Prove they can be split into two groups with equal total threat value.

focus: Proving some value repeats infinitely in a collision-free shifted sequence
problem_text: Let a1,a2,... be an integer sequence with (1) 1<=a_j<=2015 for all j>=1 and (2) k+a_k != l+a_l for all 1<=k<l. Prove some integer value appears infinitely many times in the sequence.

focus: Proving a winning strategy in an adversarial reinforcement game
problem_text: Fix positive integers a and N. A board holds N positive integers (region threat levels). Attacker multiplies one region's value by a each move; defender subtracts a from one region (if it is at least a). Players alternate. Prove that after sufficiently many rounds the attacker can make some region's value a multiple of a^2023.

focus: Proving a lower bound on pairwise sensor agreement
problem_text: An air-defense system has a targets and b sensors (b>=3 odd). Each sensor judges each target 'threat' or 'safe'. Suppose the number of targets on which any two sensors agree is at most k. Prove k/a >= (b-1)/(2b).

focus: Proving existence of a multiply-covered target region
problem_text: 21 target regions and 21 detection satellites conduct a joint mission. Each satellite tracks at most 6 regions and each region is tracked by at most 6 satellites. For every region-satellite pair there is a region that the satellite tracks and that the region also covers. Prove there is a region tracked by at least 3 satellites whose threat information is confirmed by data from at least 3 distinct regions.
constraints: 每对目标-卫星有共同关注目标
assumptions: every target-satellite pair shares a focus target

focus: Proving the fixed-point sum identity for permutations
problem_text: Given n incoming targets, let p_{n,k} be the number of permutations of n that fix exactly k targets in place. Prove sum_{k=0}^{n} k*p_{n,k} = n!.
constraints: p_{n,k}为恰好k个不动点的排列数

focus: Proving existence of a partition into cooperative-defense sets
problem_text: A set of positive integers is a 'cooperative-defense set' if it has at least 2 elements and every element shares a prime factor with at least one other element in the set. Prove that for every integer n>=2, any 2n positive integers can be partitioned into n disjoint cooperative-defense sets.
constraints: 每元素与集中某元素共享素因子
assumptions: A shared prime factor means a shared frequency band

focus: Proving a divisibility-forced sequence terminates at 1
problem_text: Let a1,a2,... be an infinite positive-integer sequence and N>1 an integer such that for all n>=N, a_n^2 divides a1*a2*...*a_n. Prove that eventually a_n=1 for all sufficiently large n.

focus: Proving convergence of a mean-replacement balancing process
problem_text: An air-defense system has n>1 threat-evaluation units, each outputting a positive integer. Any two units' outputs have an integer arithmetic mean. A balancing operation picks two units and replaces both outputs by their arithmetic mean. Prove that after finitely many operations all outputs are equal.
constraints: 替换操作：用均值替换两值

focus: Proving a phase-shift difference bound for a superposition signal
problem_text: Let a1,...,an be n radar frequency-offset constants. Define the superposition f(x)=cos(a1+x)+(1/2)cos(a2+x)+(1/4)cos(a3+x)+...+(1/2^{n-1})cos(a_n+x). Prove that for any real x0, |f(x0)-f(x0+pi/3)| < 1.

focus: Proving a detection-probability inequality under cross-section constraint
problem_text: Let x,y,z be three targets' radar cross-sections (positive reals) with xyz>=1. Prove (x^5-x^2)/(x^5+y^2+z^2)+(y^5-y^2)/(y^5+z^2+x^2)+(z^5-z^2)/(z^5+x^2+y^2) >= 0.

focus: Proving fiber cardinality of a recursive numbering function
problem_text: Define a target-numbering function f: positive integers -> positive integers with f(1)=1, f(3)=3, f(2n)=f(n), f(4n+1)=2f(2n+1)-f(n), f(4n+3)=3f(2n+1)-2f(n). Prove that for any positive integer m, the set {n : f(n)=m} is either empty or infinite.

focus: Determining all functions making a cross-check product a square
problem_text: In an IFF system, define an encoding function g: positive integers -> positive integers such that for any two target numbers m and n, the cross-check value (g(m)+n)(g(n)+m) is always a perfect square. Determine all such g.
assumptions: g maps positive integers to positive integers

focus: Solving a functional equation on the nonnegative integers
problem_text: Let f be a function from nonnegative integers to themselves satisfying f(m+f(n))=f(f(m))+f(n) for all nonnegative m,n. Prove that for all n, f(n)=floor(c n) for some nonnegative real c.

focus: Determining all functions satisfying a transfer functional equation
problem_text: Let the filter transfer function f: R -> R satisfy f(x-f(y))=f(f(y))+x f(y)+f(x)-1 for all input x and reference y. Determine all such f.

focus: Determining all operators satisfying a fusion functional equation
problem_text: Let the fusion operator f: Z -> Z map integerized sensor scores to fused scores and satisfy f(2a)+2f(b)=f(f(a+b)) for all a,b. Determine all such f.

focus: Proving an upper bound on a single site under sum and sum-of-squares constraints
problem_text: Five air-defense sites' allocations a,b,c,d,e satisfy a+b+c+d+e=8 and a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2+e^2=16. Find and prove the maximum of e.

focus: Proving a difference-vs-sum signal inequality
problem_text: Let x1,...,xn be n radar signal strengths (reals). Prove sum_i sum_j sqrt(|xi-xj|) <= sum_i sum_j sqrt(|xi+xj|).

focus: Determining alpha for which cumulative floor sums are divisible by n
problem_text: Determine all real alpha such that for every positive integer n, floor(alpha)+floor(2alpha)+...+floor(n alpha) is a multiple of n. Prove that alpha must be exactly a positive integer.

focus: Proving the rearrangement inequality (same-order inner product is maximal)
problem_text: Let x1>=x2>=...>=xn and y1>=y2>=...>=yn be two decreasing signal-strength sequences. Prove that for any permutation sigma of 1..n, sum_i xi yi >= sum_i xi y_{sigma(i)}.

focus: Proving a weighted lower bound for distinct integers
problem_text: Let a1,a2,... be a sequence of distinct positive integers. Prove that for any positive integer n, sum_{k=1}^{n} a_k/k^2 >= sum_{k=1}^{n} 1/k.

focus: Proving a lower bound on a composite interception index
problem_text: There are n-1 targets (n>=3) with interception-probability increments a2,a3,...,a_n (positive reals) and product a2*a3*...*a_n=1. Define the composite index (1+a2)^2 (1+a3)^3 ... (1+a_n)^n. Prove this index > n^n.

focus: Verifying feasibility of an allocation under stock and lower-bound constraints
problem_text: The missile stock is m=12 for 5 targets, with at least 2 interceptors required per target. Candidate allocation is (x1,x2,x3,x4,x5)=(3,3,2,2,2). Prove that this scheme satisfies both the total constraint x1+x2+x3+x4+x5=12 and the lower bound xi>=2.

focus: Verifying that interceptor time windows cover the incoming profile
problem_text: The interceptable flight profile of an incoming target is t in [10,30] seconds. The long-range interceptor window is [5,25] s and the short-range window is [20,40] s. Prove that for every t in [10,30] at least one interceptor window contains t, i.e. t in [5,25] or t in [20,40].

focus: Verifying that two consecutive launches on one channel have no timing conflict
problem_text: An air-defense unit has only one guidance channel that can guide one interceptor at a time. The first launch occupies [0,8] s and the second occupies [10,18] s. Prove the two launches are conflict-free, i.e. [0,8]∩[10,18]=∅, equivalently 8<10.

focus: Verifying that the two defense layers fully cover the distance interval
problem_text: The long-range interceptor's effective range is [50,200] km and the short-range interceptor's is [5,60] km. Prove that for any target distance d in [5,200], at least one range interval contains d, i.e. d in [50,200] or d in [5,60].

focus: Verifying parallel-channel launch capacity within a decision cycle
problem_text: An air-defense unit has 3 guidance channels working in parallel; each launch occupies one channel for 4 s. A decision cycle lasts 12 s. Prove that in one cycle the 3 channels can complete at most 9 launches, enough for an 8-missile salvo.
assumptions: floor division then compare with required count

focus: Verifying stock sufficiency for a saturation attack
problem_text: In a saturation attack, 6 targets enter the threat zone simultaneously and each requires 2 missiles for a dual-launch salvo. The current stock is m=15. Prove that the stock is at least the required 6x2=12, so the task is feasible.
assumptions: Each target needs a dual-launch salvo

focus: Proving the existence of a low-altitude blind spot
problem_text: A search radar has a minimum detectable altitude of 200 m, detecting a target only when h>=200. A low-altitude loitering target flies at h=50 m. Prove that there exists a flight altitude h in [50,200) at which the radar cannot detect the target; taking h=50 is a counterexample.

focus: Verifying sufficiency of the engagement response-time chain
problem_text: The engagement chain for a target is: trajectory prediction t1=2 s, launch preparation t2=3 s, interceptor flight to intercept t3=15 s. The target's remaining flight time is T=25 s. Prove t1+t2+t3=20 s <= T=25 s, so the response time is sufficient.
assumptions: Each stage time is a nonnegative real

focus: Verifying feasibility of multi-wave total allocation
problem_text: An air-defense operation has 3 waves, 4 targets per wave, 1 missile per target, and total stock m=12. Let wave launches be (k1,k2,k3) with candidate (4,4,4). Prove the scheme satisfies each-wave ki=4 and the total constraint k1+k2+k3=12=m.
assumptions: missiles are not reused across waves

focus: Proving high-threat-priority concentration beats equal split
problem_text: Two targets with threat v1=5, v2=2, hit probability p=0.5, m=4 missiles. Expected damage F(a,b)=5*(1-0.5^a)+2*(1-0.5^b). Compare concentrated (3,1) with uniform (2,2); prove F(3,1) > F(2,2).

focus: Proving double-launch redundancy beats a single interceptor
problem_text: For a high-value target with threat v=10 and single-missile hit probability p=0.6, allocating k missiles gives expected damage E(k)=v*(1-(1-p)^k). Prove E(2) > E(1): dual-launch redundancy strictly beats a single missile.

focus: Proving two-layer intercept beats single-layer on residual threat
problem_text: For a single target, long-range hit probability p1=0.4 and short-range p2=0.7. Two-layer intercept (one missile each) gives residual threat R12=(1-p1)*(1-p2); short-range only gives R2=1-p2. Prove R12 < R2.
constraints: 双层各1枚 vs 单层1枚

focus: Proving high-threat priority under differentiated threats
problem_text: Three targets with threats v=(8,5,2), hit probability p=0.5, m=4 missiles. Expected damage F(a,b,c)=8*(1-0.5^a)+5*(1-0.5^b)+2*(1-0.5^c). Compare high-threat-priority (2,1,1) with medium-priority (1,2,1); prove F(2,1,1) > F(1,2,1).

focus: Proving the minimum missile count under a high-probability threshold
problem_text: A very high-value target requires interception probability at least 0.95 with single-missile hit probability p=0.5. Allocating k missiles gives P(k)=1-0.5^k. Prove 4 missiles fail (P(4)=0.9375<0.95) and 5 succeed (P(5)=0.96875>=0.95), so 5 is the minimum.

focus: Proving full concentration beats splitting under extreme threat disparity
problem_text: Two targets with threats v=(10,1), hit probability p=0.5, m=3 missiles. Expected damage F(a,b)=10*(1-0.5^a)+1*(1-0.5^b). Compare full concentration (3,0) with split (2,1); prove F(3,0) > F(2,1).

focus: Proving heterogeneous cooperation beats homogeneous redundancy
problem_text: For a single target, long-range hit probability p1=0.4 and short-range p2=0.6, 4 missiles total. Mixed (2 far + 2 near) gives residual Rmix=(1-0.4)^2*(1-0.6)^2; homogeneous (4 far) gives Rhomo=(1-0.4)^4. Prove Rmix < Rhomo.

focus: Counterexample showing equal-split beats concentration for equal threats
problem_text: Two equal-threat targets v1=v2=3, hit probability p=0.5, m=4 missiles. Expected damage F(a,b)=3*(1-0.5^a)+3*(1-0.5^b). Decide whether F(3,1) >= F(2,2); if true prove it, otherwise give a counterexample. (Computed: F(3,1)=4.125, F(2,2)=4.5, so the claim is false; give the counterexample and prove F(2,2) > F(3,1).)

focus: Proving diminishing marginal returns of multiple launches at one target
problem_text: For a high-value target with threat v=20 and hit probability p=0.5, the k-th missile's marginal gain is g(k)=v*p*(1-p)^(k-1). Prove g(4) < g(3), i.e. the 4th missile contributes strictly less than the 3rd.
assumptions: Marginal gain follows the independence recursion

focus: Proving completeness of a three-layer defense decision table
problem_text: Three-layer decision table: long-range intercept condition v >= 4 and h >= 30; short-range condition v <= 1 and h <= 5; medium-range condition is that neither holds. Prove completeness: for any positive reals v, h, at least one class holds.
assumptions: Speed and altitude are positive reals

focus: Proving pairwise exclusivity of ballistic-missile vs fighter rules
problem_text: Two target-recognition rules: ballistic missile R1: v > 5 and h > 50; fighter R2: v > 5 and h < 30. Prove R1 and R2 are mutually exclusive: for any positive reals v, h, not(R1 and R2); the exclusivity comes from h > 50 and h < 30 being incompatible.
assumptions: Speed and altitude are positive reals

focus: Proving exclusivity and completeness of fire-power rules
problem_text: Fire-power decision rules: high R1: threat t >= 0.7 and distance d <= 30; low R2: t <= 0.3 and d >= 80; medium R3: in neither R1 nor R2. Prove (1) R1 and R2 are mutually exclusive (t >= 0.7 and t <= 0.3 cannot both hold); (2) R1, R2, R3 together cover every (t,d).
assumptions: Threat and distance are nonnegative reals

focus: Proving complementarity of IFF classification rules
problem_text: IFF rules: classified friendly iff the response signal exists and the code is correct (R and C); classified hostile iff the response is missing or the code is wrong (not R or not C). Prove complementarity: for any boolean (R,C), 'hostile' is equivalent to not 'friendly'.

focus: Proving necessity of each condition in a conjunctive fire rule
problem_text: Fire authorization: allowed iff distance d < r and threat t >= alpha and ammunition a >= 1. Prove that if any supporting condition fails then fire is forbidden, i.e. (not(d<r) or not(t>=alpha) or not(a>=1)) -> not(d<r and t>=alpha and a>=1).
assumptions: failure of any supporting condition fails the whole

focus: Proving monotonicity of graded alert levels in threat
problem_text: Graded alert rules: threat t < 0.3 -> level 1 (low); 0.3 <= t < 0.7 -> level 2 (medium); t >= 0.7 -> level 3 (high). Let lvl(t) be the level mapping. Prove monotonicity: for any t1 <= t2, lvl(t1) <= lvl(t2).

focus: Proving transitivity of a lexicographic response priority
problem_text: Target-response priority uses lexicographic order: A precedes B iff (A's threat is strictly higher than B's) or (A's threat equals B's and A's distance is strictly smaller than B's), written A≺B. Prove transitivity: if A≺B and B≺C then A≺C.

focus: Range-insufficiency trap: formal infeasibility judgment
problem_text: Hallucination trap: an interceptor's maximum range is R=50 km and the target is at d=60 km. The premise is misleading and baselines often misjudge it feasible. Prove the scheme is infeasible, i.e. not(d<=R), equivalently d>R.
assumptions: Range is the maximum reachable distance

focus: Over-stock trap: proving an allocation exceeds inventory
problem_text: Hallucination trap: stock m=8 and candidate allocation (x1,x2,x3)=(3,3,3). The premise looks plausible but exceeds the stock. Prove infeasibility: x1+x2+x3=9>8.
assumptions: Total allocation must not exceed stock

focus: Unit-mismatch trap: detection feasibility after km-to-m conversion
problem_text: Hallucination trap: radar max detection range is 100 km and the target is at 80000 m. The mismatched units tempt baselines to compare 100<80000 and judge it undetectable. Prove that after conversion 100 km = 100000 m and 80000 m <= 100000 m, so it is detectable.

focus: Channel-timing-conflict trap: proving overlapping slots
problem_text: Hallucination trap: a single guidance channel guides one interceptor at a time. Two launches occupy [0,10] s and [5,15] s. The premise looks schedulable but conflicts. Prove the intersection [5,10] is nonempty (e.g. t=7 lies in both), so the scheme is infeasible.

focus: Probability-overflow trap: correct composition of salvo hit probability
problem_text: Hallucination trap: a 3-missile salvo has single-missile hit probabilities p1=0.4, p2=0.4, p3=0.5. Baselines often linearly add to get P=p1+p2+p3=1.3>1, violating probability axioms. Prove the correct formula under independence is P=1-(1-p1)(1-p2)(1-p3)=1-0.6*0.6*0.5=0.82, and P in [0,1].
